A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SINKTRACK and contain 17 readable pages, including the main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results in Tables 1–2, injection ablations, qualitative comparisons, and appendix measurements of attention stability and computational overhead.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, ablation, qualitative, attention-stability, and latency results.

M1.justification: Sections 2.2–2.4 and Algorithm S1 retain the same hard/soft injection exploration and final dual-track cross-attention procedure, including use of unpooled contextual features.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RealWorldQA, MMStar, M3CoT, POPE, QuAC, and SQuAD2.0, including the same QuAC subsets and appendix test scenarios.

E2.justification: Direct prompting and CoT remain the evaluated baselines in Tables 1–2, and the injection variants are unchanged. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported models, sample counts, accuracy/Macro-F1 metrics, injection intervals, and drift-test and latency procedures remain unchanged. Table S1's isolated sequence-position correction does not indicate a redesigned protocol.

E4.justification: The pooling and injection ablations, qualitative cases, attention-flow analysis, hierarchical-attention comparison, and long-generation stability test are retained. No analysis is added or substantively revised; the isolated Table S1 correction is covered under E6.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and report mean ± variance in Section 3.2. The Spearman correlation and significance reporting in Section 3.4.2 and Appendix B.1 are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Table S1 changes the sequence position at generated-token index 128 from 5210 to 8210. Its attention values and ratio remain unchanged, as do the benchmark scores, ablation results, latency measurements, and qualitative findings.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), their mathematical formulations, and the algorithmic definitions are retained. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free context anchoring through attention sinks, mitigation of hallucination and context forgetting, negligible overhead, and generalization across models and modalities.

C2.justification: The explanations involving preserved computational flow, contextual information delivery, and CoT failures remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the same single-anchor information bottleneck and limitations for very long or dense contexts.

D1.justification: Algorithm S1, every-five-layer injection details, RTX 4090 latency setup, and code-access information are unchanged. The pseudocode's visual formatting changes without altering its technical content.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces three background references with six others, and Section 4 adds citations to Wang et al. (2025), Lei et al. (2024), Weng et al. (2025), and Li et al. (2025a). Citation coverage changes, but the related-work taxonomy and SINKTRACK's novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 changes from 'Experimental Setting' to 'Experimental Setup'; Sections 3.2 and 3.3 pluralize 'Comparison Result' to 'Comparison Results.' The narrative and section organization otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Algorithm S1's input-description block receives teal comment styling and loses visible space markers. Citation edits cause limited prose and bibliography reflow; the figures, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table S1's sequence position from 5210 to 8210 removes an internal inconsistency with the surrounding rows and the stated 8k+ input context. Small heading and pseudocode-formatting edits also improve presentation. These are limited gains in reporting quality; the scientific contribution, measured outcomes, and limitations remain essentially unchanged.
